subject: Capacity forecast + OEM lead-time alignment for Q3 committed deals
messages:
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@cloudway.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-12T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity conversation — rough timing and lead times

Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Quick follow-up from our procurement side: FintechCo is aiming to finalize committed capacity numbers by 11/25 so they can hit their internal board approval. They asked us to confirm two things from you all:

1) A realistic delivery lead time for reserved GPU capacity (H100-equivalent) if we go the OEM purchase + colocation route vs. cloud-reserved instances with CloudWay.
2) Any constraints or minimums on model variant pinning / quantization profile that would affect how quickly you can bring customers online on Dedicated.

We have a preliminary requirement of ~320 effective H100-equivalent slots (usable inference lanes) across two regions (us-west/us-east) with an initial ramp plan. Attached is our draft forecast. Appreciate any concrete timing and whether we should prioritize OEM purchase now vs. pulling cloud reserved capacity.

Attachments: Forecast_Q3_capacity.xlsx (spreadsheet)

—Alex
Alex Jenkins
Enterprise Sales, CloudWay Solutions
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@cloudway.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-12T12:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity conversation — rough timing and lead times

Alex — thanks, received. Looping Karthik (infra capacity) and Marissa (customer success / commercial) to align. High level thoughts:

- OEM purchase (bare-metal or dedicated boxes) gives the best unit economics long term but OEM lead times for H100-class hardware are currently 14–20 weeks depending on config and country of fulfillment. Procurement and staging typically add 2–4 weeks. So realistic OEM-to-production is ~16–24 weeks start-to-serve.

- Cloud reserved capacity (CloudWay or major CSP reserved instances) is much faster to stand up (2–4 weeks to reserve, plus 1–2 weeks to provision and test). Unit cost is higher but you get immediate runway and flexibility while OEM orders arrive.

- For model variant pinning: if FintechCo requires pinned older FP16-only variants, we can bring those online faster; any custom quantization or N:M sparse optimizations require a brief model onboarding window (~3–5 business days) and might affect scheduling.

I’ll pull together a short plan: immediate 12–16 week runway using reserved cloud to cover onboarding + canary, followed by OEM arrival to lower unit cost and scale. Karthik — can you confirm 320 effective H100-equivalent mapping to our node types and any advice on how to size burst vs steady pools?

Soojin Lee
Lead, Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-13T08:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity conversation — rough timing and lead times

Soojin / Marissa — dug into the numbers using the FintechCo forecast. Quick notes:

- "320 H100-equivalent slots" translates to roughly: 80 NVidia H100-80GB GPUs if you use 4 effective slots per GPU (depending heavily on batching/prompt length). If they expect larger seq lengths or high concurrency we should plan for ~100 GPUs to be safe.

- For OEM order: lead times vary by vendor. Our standard OEM partner (OEMCo) quoted 16 weeks for H100-80GB cabinets today but warned that queueing for 2026 Q1 fulfillment could push to 20 weeks. Shipping and customs add country-dependent buffer (7–14 days).

- For cloud reservations: CloudWay quoted a 3-week lead to reservation confirmation plus up to 10 business days for provisioning and network peering for private deployments. They have a handful of regional capacity pools we can tap into but for sustained committed capacity they require a 12–18 month financial commitment to get the best unit rates.

- Sizing recommendation: start with 40 reserved nodes (cloud) covering the onboarding + canary and provision 80–100 OEM GPUs for steady-state. Configure autoscale to burst to a shared pool (hosted fallback) for spikes.

I attached a short mapping I used. (attachment: OEM_quote_NVIDIA_H100_v2.pdf)

—Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@cloudway.com>, Nina Park <nina.park@fintechco.com>
Date: 2025-11-14T10:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity forecast + OEM lead-time alignment for Q3 committed deals

Adding some commercial constraints from FintechCo’s side (I spoke to Nina):

- They want the procurement plan to show cost/runway scenarios: (A) cloud-reserved-only for first 6 months; (B) hybrid (cloud + OEM arrival month 4); (C) straight OEM (if we can guarantee earlier delivery).
- Finance needs a sample contract addendum showing start-of-billing tied to a 'ready-for-production' checklist (network peering, SST tests passed, observability hooks configured). If OEM arrives later, they expect billing to start on a mutually-agreed service activation date, not shipment date.
- They asked if Redwood can commit to a fallback policy (e.g., switch to a smaller model when capacity constrained) and an SLO for mean token latency under typical load. Can we formalize that for the doc?

Planning ask: can Karthik and Dev produce the two scenarios (hybrid & cloud-only) with expected unit cost and activation timelines by EOD Friday? I’ll consolidate and send to their procurement team.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@cloudway.com>, Nina Park <nina.park@fintechco.com>, OEM Sales <nvidia-sales@oemco.com>
Date: 2025-11-17T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity forecast + OEM lead-time alignment for Q3 committed deals

Team — attaching the initial cost/time scenarios for the two asks. Highlights:

- Scenario A (Cloud-reserved-only, 6 months): provisioning in 3 weeks, monthly run rate ~1.9x OEM unit cost; total 6-month spend ~ $2.1M (ballpark) for 320 effective slots across two regions.
- Scenario B (Hybrid): Cloud reservations to cover months 0–3 (40 reserved nodes), OEM order placed immediately; OEM arrival month ~16–20 weeks; blended unit cost reduces overall 12-month spend by ~35% vs cloud-only.
- Billing proposal: activation = completion of pre-prod checklist (network peering, canary pass, security attestations). We proposed a 30-day SLA credit if activation misses agreed date due to Redwood-side capacity issues.

Attachments: CloudWay_capacity_pricing.xlsx

Next steps I recommend:
1) We share the hybrid scenario workbook with FintechCo procurement and OEM Sales concurrently.
2) Alex / CloudWay confirm regional pool capacity and timeline (Alex, can you confirm week-of-provisioning availability once we submit PO?).
3) OEM Sales, please confirm whether you can support an earlier partial shipment (e.g., deliver racks to colos in phased waves) to shorten customer activation time.

—Dev
Head of Capacity Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@cloudway.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Park <nina.park@fintechco.com>
Date: 2025-11-19T16:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity forecast + OEM lead-time alignment for Q3 committed deals

Team — thanks for the breakdown and the workbook. Quick confirmations:

- CloudWay can confirm provisional availability in us-west for the requested 40 reserved nodes week-of 2025-12-08, pending PO and network peering window. Full us-east pool availability requires a signed commitment by 2025-12-05 to hold the capacity.
- We can support phased provisioning; we recommend a 2-wave approach: 24 nodes in wave 1, remaining 16 in wave 2.
- I’ve asked OEM Sales (cc'ed) for visibility on phased OEM shipments. They indicated in thread they'll try to accommodate but need PO + configuration sign-off to prioritize the order.

I’ll follow up with a short mutually-agreed MAP (mutual action plan) doc and a tentative timeline for the next 90 days.

—Alex
Enterprise Sales, CloudWay Solutions
